cover.headline: A cash-rich B2B platform priced for decline: the customer base has stalled, but at ~16x forward EPS the de-rating has run ahead of the peers
cover.lead: IndiaMART is India's largest B2B marketplace: 2.2 lakh MSME suppliers pay it subscriptions for buyer leads, in advance. Q1FY27 revenue rose 11% and the EBITDA margin was 35%, but paying suppliers fell for a third quarter (218K) and buyer enquiries are flat; the stock is down 15% since the results and 59% below its five-year median P/E. We forecast EPS of ₹90.3 / ₹103.0 / ₹118.0 for FY27-29E, within ~3% of MOSL and Choice. The street values IndiaMART on **P/E on FY28E** (Choice 20x; MOSL's DCF ≈ 21x). On the house rule we start from its own one-year-forward P/E median since Apr-2021 on EPS before start-up fair-value gains (36.1x) and apply the sector move of the internet and online-classifieds names with a usable five-year history (Info Edge, Just Dial, Matrimony.com: median −37%). **22.5x Sep-28E EPS of ₹110.5 = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with BUY.** The street median is ₹2,060; on the last two years' multiples alone the value is ₹1,770, which is the bear argument in one number. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: Growth is all price now, and that has limits
arguments.p: Paying suppliers were 217K at Mar-25 and 218K at Jun-26; ARPU rose from ₹61K to ₹69K. Platinum and Gold (half the base, >75% of revenue) renew and upgrade; Silver churns ~7% a month, and the Q2FY26 Silver price rise cut gross additions. Management will not buy growth until renewals improve. We assume ~10% revenue growth from ARPU, no customer recovery.

arguments.h: A high-margin cash machine with a third of its value in cash
arguments.p: Customers prepay (deferred revenue ₹2,014 cr), capex is negligible and the company has no debt: ₹3,553 cr of cash and treasury (~₹590 a share) plus ₹741 cr of start-up stakes. EBITDA margin ~33.7% (company basis); FY26 payout 76%. Excluding its cash and stakes (~₹711 a share) and their income, the stock trades at ~12.8x FY28E operating EPS.

arguments.h: Reported EPS is noisy; we value it before the noise
arguments.p: Other income is a third of pre-tax profit and swings with bond marks (−₹34 cr in Q4FY26, +₹107 cr in Q1FY27); fair-value gains on 13 start-up stakes added up to a fifth of EPS (FY23). Associates' losses (₹55 cr) sit inside Screener's EBITDA. We forecast a normal 7% treasury return and no start-up gains, and derive the multiple on EPS before them.

arguments.h: Valuation: the de-rating has gone further than at its peers
arguments.p: IndiaMART trades 59% below its five-year median P/E; Info Edge (−38%), Just Dial (−37%) and Matrimony.com (−12%) less. The house multiple (22.5x) assumes IndiaMART recovers to its history less the peers' de-rating. That is the upside, and the risk: if AI search erodes buyer enquiries, part of the de-rating is permanent.

bullets: **Per-share data are bonus-adjusted.** The 1:1 bonus in Q1FY24 doubled the share count to ~6.0 crore; Screener and this report show EPS and prices on the post-bonus basis.

**The FY21 QIP is why the balance sheet is cash-heavy.** Cash and treasury rose from ₹931 cr to ₹2,365 cr in FY21 and has grown to ₹3,553 cr since, despite ~₹1,220 cr of strategic investments and ~₹1,650 cr of capital returned.
**Busy changed the mix and added goodwill.** ₹454 cr of goodwill since FY23; Busy's FY26 revenue (+80%) is flattered by the switch to subscription billing (normalised ~44%).

**One-offs in reported profit:** fair-value gains on strategic stakes of ₹84 cr (FY23), ₹29 cr (FY24), ₹43 cr (FY25) and ₹78 cr (FY26), and a ₹29 cr gain on selling an associate stake in FY25. We strip them out of the EPS history used for valuation.

sections.title: Indian B2B discovery: a big MSME base, half of it already on IndiaMART, and a new gatekeeper in AI search

blocks.p: ~1.6 crore GST-registered businesses (about half with turnover below Rs40 lakh, 85% proprietorships); ~50 lakh GST-identified sellers registered on IndiaMART, 2.2 lakh paying; management puts free-tier penetration of the serviceable market at ~50% (Q4FY26 call). IndiaMART is a classifieds-style marketplace, not a transaction platform: it does not take a commission on the deal, hold inventory or handle payment (a buyer-payment protection programme for TrustSEAL sellers started in 2026). It sells visibility and buy leads to suppliers on annual and multi-year subscriptions. Survey data: ~40-45% of buyers who respond say they procured through IndiaMART; 90-day buyer repeat rate 58-59% (up from 50-51%) (Q1FY27 call).

blocks.p: IndiaMART stopped reporting traffic about a year before Q1FY27 because bot, agent and LLM traffic made it hard to classify; it spends Rs7-8 cr a quarter on buyer advertising in its top-10% categories and is moving to 100% OTP buyer verification behind log-in (Q1FY27 call). The new threat is AI assistants answering procurement queries without sending traffic to listing sites: management calls it 'a two-way sword' (Q1FY27 call).

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict: a moat, but a narrowing one.** IndiaMART is the default B2B listing site in India and its best customers pay more every year, which is what a moat looks like. But a moat should also show in volumes: buyer enquiries have been flat for several quarters and the paying base has not grown for two years. If AI assistants become the place where Indian buyers start a procurement search, IndiaMART's data stays valuable but its control of the lead weakens. We score the moat as moderate, with the direction of travel negative until enquiries grow again.

sections.title: Revenue up 2.3x in five years; the margin fell in FY23-24, recovered in FY25 and has been flat since

blocks.p: Consolidated revenue grew from ₹670 cr in FY21 to ₹1,569 cr in FY26 (19% a year), almost all of it from the marketplace: IndiaMART standalone ₹665 cr to ₹1,443 cr, Busy (bought in FY23) ₹119 cr in FY26. The margin story has three acts. In FY21 Covid froze hiring and marketing and the EBITDA margin (company basis, before associates) hit 49%. In FY23-24 management spent to grow: headcount and sales teams went up, the paying-supplier base rose from 169K to 214K, and the margin fell to 27-28%. In FY25 it stopped chasing customers who churned, cut acquisition costs and raised prices: margin back to 38%, ~34% in FY26 and 35% in Q1FY27. Revenue growth slowed from 31% (FY23) to 13% (FY26) and 11% (Q1FY27) because the number of paying suppliers stopped growing (217K at Mar-25, 218K at Jun-26). Since FY25 growth has come from price (ARPU ₹61K to ₹69K), not customers.

sections.title: Earnings quality: cash-backed operating profit, but reported EPS is moved by bond marks and start-up revaluations

bullets: **Cash comes first.** Customers pay before revenue is booked: cash from operations was ₹694 cr in FY26, 146% of (Screener) EBITDA and 146% of net profit; deferred revenue grew ₹287 cr in the year.

**Other income is half real return, half noise.** FY26 other income of ₹204.1 cr = ₹112.9 cr of treasury return (after a bond mark-to-market loss in Q4) + ₹9.1 cr of interest + ₹77.7 cr of fair-value gains on start-ups + ₹4.4 cr of write-backs. We build FY27E as 7% on opening net treasury (₹4,020 cr, incl. ₹763 cr of stakes) less ₹50 cr for the non-yielding stakes and write-backs = ₹{{F.otherIncome.0|num}} cr, against ₹126 cr in FY26 and ₹141 cr in the twelve months to Jun-26 before start-up gains (₹218 cr reported). Q1FY27 alone gave ₹107 cr as bond yields eased.
**Associates' losses sit inside EBITDA on Screener.** ₹54.8 cr in FY26; the company reports EBITDA before them (₹530 cr) and Screener after (₹475 cr). Our model follows Screener; we quote both.
**ESOP cost is real and rising:** ₹36.6 cr in FY26 (₹18.7 cr in FY25), 2.3% of revenue; management highlights "adjusted EBITDA" before it. We deduct it.
**Tax:** 26.7% in FY26 vs 22.0% in FY25 (FY25 had lower-taxed capital gains); associates' losses are not deductible.
**Revenue recognition is conservative:** subscription fees are recognised over the period; ~62% of deferred revenue falls due within a year, the rest is multi-year.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: GREEN, with a caveat on reported EPS.** Unqualified audit, no debt, cash ahead of revenue. The caveat is presentation: one-third of pre-tax profit is other income, and up to a fifth of EPS in a year has come from revaluing start-up stakes. Judge the company on operating profit plus a normal treasury return, which is what we forecast.

sections.title: No debt, ₹3,553 cr of cash and treasury, ₹741 cr of start-up stakes, and customers' money in advance

blocks.p: At Mar-2026 IndiaMART held ₹3,280 cr of cash and treasury investments (debt mutual funds, bonds, ETFs, InvITs, deposits) and ₹763 cr of strategic investments (associates at equity, other start-ups at fair value), against ₹23 cr of lease liabilities and no borrowings. Goodwill of ₹454 cr (Busy, Livekeeping) is most of the fixed assets. The biggest liability is deferred revenue (₹1,965 cr): subscriptions paid for but not yet delivered, ~62% due within twelve months. At Jun-2026 treasury was ₹3,553 cr (~₹590 a share, 36% of the 30-Sep-2026 share price); the strategic stakes add ~₹125 a share at book.

sections.title: Our honest summary: 14.7x Sep-28E EPS for a stalled but cash-rich platform; BUY, if the multiple recovers part of its de-rating

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's largest B2B listing platform: 2.2 lakh paying MSME suppliers, an ARPU that has risen 57% in four years, a ~34% EBITDA margin, no debt, ₹3,553 cr of cash and treasury (~₹590 a share) and customers who pay up to years in advance. Also a ₹750 cr start-up portfolio and Busy, which add noise more than value today.

**What you are paying:** 18.0x our FY27E and 14.7x Sep-28E EPS, ~12.8x FY28E operating EPS after its cash and stakes. Since 2021 the market has paid a median 36.1x forward (before one-offs). On the street's method and the house multiple the target is {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): BUY. With the last two years' multiples only it would be ~₹1,770; with classifieds peers only ~₹2,980; the DCF says ~₹3,166. The street median is ₹2,060.

**This is a multiple call, and we say so.** Our EPS is within ~3% of the street's. The house rule takes IndiaMART's own forward P/E median before one-offs (36.1x) and applies the three-name sector move (−37%): 22.5x. IndiaMART has de-rated by −59% against its five-year median, more than its peers, which is why the rule finds upside. Part of that de-rating is deserved (two years without customer growth, AI risk to discovery), which the rule does not capture: on the last two years' multiples the value is ~₹1,770.
**We would move to HOLD above ~₹2,160** and to SELL above ~₹2,610 on today's numbers, or sooner if paying suppliers keep falling and enquiries decline.
**Biggest swing factors:** the multiple (each 1x is ~₹111 a share), the paying-supplier trend and the standalone margin (each point is ~₹16 cr of EBITDA).

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for IndiaMART InterMESH (consolidated, Rs crore). Segment model by legal entity, as the company reports it: IndiaMART standalone (the B2B marketplace, adjusted EBITDA before ESOP cost), Busy Infotech (accounting software) and Others (other subsidiaries and inter-company items, revenue only). EBITDA = segments - unallocated - ESOP, where unallocated = share of associates' losses (Screener deducts it inside expenses, so the model EBITDA equals Screener operating profit) + the EBITDA loss of the other subsidiaries. Valued on P/E, as the street does; the multiple is derived in tools/authoring/INDIAMART.ctx.js and written here by INDIAMART.val.js.

segments.name: IndiaMART (marketplace, standalone)
segments._why: Revenue = paying suppliers x ARPU, recognised from deferred revenue. FY26 +9.3% (suppliers 217K to 220K, ARPU Rs61K to Rs66K); Q1FY27 +9% with suppliers flat YoY at 218K (net -1.85K QoQ, Silver churn ~7% a month) and ARPU +8% to Rs69K. Standalone collections +10% in FY26 and +8% in Q1FY27; deferred revenue +14% YoY to Rs1,858 cr (~20% recognised within three months). Management guides 10-12% consolidated revenue growth for FY27 (May-2026) and gives no net-add guidance. We assume ARPU-led growth: +9.5% FY27E, +10% FY28-29E (flat to slightly rising suppliers, ARPU +8-9% a year from price increases and category-based Platinum pricing). MOSL models ~8-9% collection growth over FY27-28E.
segments._marginWhy: Standalone adjusted EBITDA margin (before ESOP): 40.2% FY25, 38.5% FY26, 41.5% Q1FY27 (lower acquisition spend; headcount -4% YoY). Management guides ~33% consolidated EBITDA (+/-1-2 pts) for FY27 and says sustained leverage needs subscriber growth; any return to gross adds raises sales cost. 39.5% flat gives ~33.8% consolidated (company basis) in FY27E, inside the guided band (MOSL 33.6%, Choice 33.3%).

segments.name: Busy Infotech (accounting software)
segments._why: Revenue Rs66 cr FY25, Rs119 cr FY26 (+80%: shift from perpetual licences to subscriptions; ~44% normalised), Q1FY27 Rs36 cr (+47%), deferred revenue Rs146 cr (+44%), billing +10% (Q1FY26 had ~Rs10 cr of one-off win-backs). Management: ~27-30% CAGR over the next couple of years (Q1FY27 call); ~25% (May-2026 interview). +32% FY27E (deferred revenue already booked), +27%, +25%.
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA margin 7% FY25, 17.6% FY26, 8% Q1FY27 (Busy Magic relaunch, product and team investment). 12% FY27E rising to 17% by FY29E as subscriptions scale; management expects improving margins.

segments.name: Others (subsidiaries, inter-company)
segments._why: Livekeeping and other small subsidiaries less inter-company items: revenue Rs2 cr FY25, Rs7 cr FY26, Rs3 cr Q1FY27.
segments._marginWhy: Their EBITDA (FY26 -Rs11 cr, Q1FY27 -Rs6 cr) is carried in the unallocated line.

assumptions._unallocLabel: Share of associates' losses + other subsidiaries' EBITDA loss
assumptions._unallocWhy: Associates (Vyapar, Mobisy/Bizom, Truckhall/SuperProcure, Fleetx and others, equity-accounted): Rs49 cr FY25, Rs55 cr FY26, Rs14.6 cr Q1FY27 -> Rs58 cr, Rs55 cr, Rs50 cr as the larger investees approach break-even. Others' EBITDA: +Rs5 cr FY25, -Rs11 cr FY26, -Rs6 cr Q1FY27 (Livekeeping; IndiaMART Finance being set up) -> -Rs24 cr, -Rs22 cr, -Rs20 cr. FY26 check: 555 + 21 - 35 (ESOP) - 66 = 475 = Screener operating profit.
assumptions._esopWhy: Standalone ESOP cost (adjusted less reported EBITDA): Rs17 cr FY25, Rs35 cr FY26, Rs7 cr Q1FY27 (consolidated FY26 Rs36.6 cr, AR note 21). Rs30-34 cr.
assumptions._capexWhy: Asset-light: cash capex Rs7-16 cr a year in FY23-26 and nil in Q1FY27 (company cash-utilisation slide). Rs10-12 cr.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation and amortisation Rs28.4 cr (AR note 23: PPE Rs4.8 cr, right-of-use Rs9.4 cr, Busy/Livekeeping intangibles Rs14.2 cr) = 4.3% of average gross block (Rs655 cr, which includes Rs454 cr of goodwill that is not amortised); Q1FY27 Rs6.4 cr. 4.0% gives ~Rs26-27 cr a year.

otherTreasury._why: Treasury inside Screener's other assets: inter-corporate deposits (loans Rs90 cr) and bank deposits in other financial assets (~Rs70 cr), so that Screener cash Rs91 cr + investments Rs3,792 cr + Rs160 cr = Rs4,043 cr = the company's cash and treasury investments (Rs3,280 cr) + strategic investments at book (Rs763 cr) at Mar-26 (Q1FY27 deck). Net of Rs23 cr of lease liabilities the engine's net treasury is Rs4,020 cr.

assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied by the engine to opening net treasury, which includes the Rs763 cr of strategic stakes (they earn no yield: see other income). Treasury income (debt funds, bonds, ETFs, InvITs at fair value, plus deposit interest) was Rs200 cr in FY25 (7.7% of average treasury of Rs2,613 cr) and Rs122 cr in FY26 (4.0% of Rs3,083 cr: bond mark-to-market loss of Rs34 cr net other income in Q4FY26, 'notional, would reverse'); Q1FY27 other income Rs107 cr, 'primarily mark-to-market gains on the treasury portfolio'. Through-the-cycle return on a high-grade debt book ~7%: 7.0% in FY27E (Q1 already booked), 6.75% after (repo 5.25%).
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Fixed items: minus the yield on the strategic stakes held inside treasury (7.0%/6.75% x Rs763 cr = -Rs53/-Rs52 cr: associates are equity-accounted and other investees are valued at fair value, not yielding) plus write-backs and interest on security deposits (~Rs3-4 cr; Rs4.4 cr FY26). Fair-value gains on strategic investments (Rs42.6 cr FY25, Rs77.7 cr FY26) and the FY25 gain on selling an associate stake (Rs29.2 cr) are one-offs and not forecast. Built FY27E other income ~Rs232 cr vs Rs204 cr reported in FY26 (Rs126 cr before strategic fair-value gains) and Rs218 cr in the twelve months to Jun-26; Q1FY27 alone Rs107 cr.
assumptions._interestWhy: Lease interest Rs2.7 cr FY26 (AR note 22, plus Rs0.3 cr on deferred consideration); Rs0.5 cr in Q1FY27. No borrowings.
assumptions._taxWhy: Effective rate on profit after associates: 26.7% FY26, 22.0% FY25 (lower-taxed capital gains), 25.8% Q1FY27. Associates' losses are not tax-deductible, so ~25% statutory becomes ~26% on our PBT.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Dividend Rs50/share for FY25 (Rs30 final + Rs20 special, 55% of EPS) and Rs60 for FY26 (Rs30 final + Rs30 special, 76%); policy: surplus capital returned by dividends or buybacks; ~40-60% of cash generated distributed over the last 3-4 years (CFO, Q4FY26 call). 60%.

dcf._tgWhy: B2B digitisation of ~1.6 crore GST-registered businesses; but the paying base is flat and AI search is a real threat to discovery: 5.5%, below nominal GDP.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~11% to 7% over 15 years (ARPU-led growth cannot compound at the current pace without customer growth).
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: Model EBITDA margin (after associates) ~30.5% in FY27E-29E; held at 30%.
